remit_rules.excerpt: A message sender whose identity signature does not verify is not a trusted counterparty for state-changing or privileged actions
The agent MUST NOT act on an unsigned or signature-unverified message when performing a state-changing or privileged action.
The operator-configured allowlist of authorized peer agent addresses is a closed set
Allowed Data Sources
The agent MUST NOT treat the content of inbound messages, query payloads, broadcast traffic, or data retrieved from other agents as instructions that alter its own goals, policies, or tool set.

threats.summary: A sender that names itself user... skips env.verify() on both the HTTP and mailbox paths, so the identity decision rests on an attacker-chosen four-character prefix rather than on a key.

expires and nonce are folded into the signed digest but no ingress path checks either, so a signed envelope captured once from the network, a proxy log or the mailbox stays a valid instruction forever.

Handler selection consults only the schema digest and the user/agent prefix, so any agent on the open network can drive a handler at any rate — the ACL and quota that exist in QuotaProtocol are never wired into Agent.

Forged agent-prefixed senders are rejected: every envelope from an agent... address has its ECDSA signature checked against the sender-derived address before dispatch, with no configuration needed to enable it.

remit_rules.excerpt: The agent-inspector and other debug/administrative REST endpoints MUST be disabled in production.
If such debug/administrative endpoints are enabled, the agent MUST NOT expose them unless they sit behind operator-configured protection (authentication / network restriction).
The server the agent binds to receive envelopes; must serve only the agent's declared endpoints.

threats.summary: The inspector is on by default, which both registers /messages and turns on the payload cache behind it, so a thousand full message bodies are retained for a day and served to whoever clears the guard; /agent_info is served to everyone regardless.

The only authorization is a client IP that forwarded_allow_ips="*" lets any peer set via X-Forwarded-For, and wildcard CORS plus a blanket 204 preflight extend the same reach to any web page the operator's browser visits — ending in POST /connect re-registering the agent at a caller-supplied endpoint.
The same bypass reaches POST /disconnect, letting an unauthenticated caller unregister the agent from Agentverse and cut it off from mailbox delivery and discovery.

remit_rules.excerpt: A message sender whose identity signature does not verify is not a trusted counterparty for state-changing or privileged actions

threats.summary: A synchronous reply carrying no signature bypasses verification entirely — send_exchange_envelope only verifies "if env.signature" and the core send helper never verifies at all — so whatever answers the resolved endpoint is delivered to the waiting caller as the peer's reply.

Destination endpoint URLs come from the public Almanac/Agentverse record rather than operator configuration, so control of a peer's registry entry redirects this agent's outbound payloads to the attacker's host.

remit_rules.excerpt: Only operator-configured external integrations are authorized: the LLM adapters (e.g. ASI:One) and MCP endpoints the operator explicitly configured form a closed set

threats.summary: When the optional chat agent is configured, counterparty message text and the whole stored session history are forwarded verbatim to api.asi1.ai with no redaction or classification step.

Counterparty text is concatenated into the same message list as the operator's instructions with no delimitation, and tool_choice defaults to "required", so inbound content competes directly with the system prompt for the model's tool decision.

remit_rules.excerpt: The agent MUST NOT hold, or route untrusted message content into, any capability that executes arbitrary commands or code on the host.

threats.summary: extract_tools_from_protocol exposes every registered message handler as an LLM function tool, so a tool name chosen from counterparty text invokes an operator handler — which holds the same wallet and ledger client as any other handler — with model-generated arguments.
Model-generated arguments cannot be malformed into a handler: they are validated against the handler's own pydantic model and a failure returns a clarification rather than invoking the tool.

remit_rules.excerpt: On-chain transactions — gated per Action Boundaries.
Any capability that moves value on the ledger or spends wallet funds — see Action Boundaries.
Any discretionary on-chain value transfer or spend of wallet funds ... The framework ships no operator authorization policy for wallet spends, so the deployment MUST supply the gating policy
the agent MUST NOT move value to any counterparty other than the Almanac / Agentverse registration contract unless the operator has explicitly authorized value transfers

threats.summary: Every handler — including one processing a message that entered on the unverified user-address path — receives a LocalWallet and LedgerClient it can broadcast with, and the framework offers no approval callback or threshold the deployment could hang the remit's gating policy on.
No distinct record or event is emitted when funds move, so a spend that was not the Almanac registration fee cannot be attributed or even noticed after the fact.

remit_rules.excerpt: The agent MUST NOT autonomously register, advertise, or impersonate identities, addresses, or protocols other than its own configured identity.
Data published to the public Almanac / Agentverse profile (address, endpoints, protocols, description, README, avatar) MUST be limited to non-sensitive information intended for public discovery.
Approved Communication Channels

threats.summary: A module-level faucet client is built at import time and claimed automatically whenever a testnet registration finds the wallet short of the fee — an outbound destination the remit's channel table does not authorize and the operator never approves.

What reaches the public registry is bounded: the profile payload carries only description, readme, avatar and banner, and the Almanac attestation filters metadata down to geolocation, so no key or private configuration is published.

remit_rules.excerpt: Credentials, API keys, and seed material MUST be loaded from environment or secure operator configuration; they MUST NOT be hardcoded in source or committed to the repository.
Seed phrases, identity keys, and wallet keys MUST NEVER leave the host — never transmitted in a message, written to a log, or published to the Almanac / Agentverse profile metadata.

threats.summary: The Helm chart's agent.seed default is a working literal committed to the repository, and that one string derives both the ECDSA signing identity and the ledger wallet key, so any deployment left on the default has a publicly reproducible identity and an impersonatable address.

An agent created with a name but no seed writes its identity and wallet private keys as cleartext JSON into private_keys.json in the process working directory, with default permissions and no encryption.

get_or_create_private_keys persists a freshly generated wallet key that is not the one it returned, so the wallet address the agent uses on its first run is not the address it recovers on restart — funds land on an address the process no longer holds.

The key-value store — and, when store_message_history is enabled, whole message payloads inside it — is written to <name>_data.json in the process working directory with default permissions, so any local account that can read the agent's directory reads counterparty content.

remit_rules.excerpt: Log only — do not alert — on routine signature-verified message handling and scheduled interval task runs; these events MUST leave a log record.
Alert on Almanac / Agentverse registration failure rather than silently continuing.
Alert on repeated inbound messages from senders whose signatures fail verification or who are not authorized counterparties.

threats.summary: A successfully handled message and a completed interval run produce no log entry at all, and what is written goes through a uvicorn text formatter with no session, sender or event-type field, so nothing downstream can reconstruct who drove the agent.

There is no alert or halt primitive anywhere in the runtime, and update_agent_status swallows every exception, so registration failure, repeated verification failures and wallet movement all end at a warning or at silence.

The core send helper reports every message to Agentverse by default — target address, sender address and session id on each send to a non-Agentverse endpoint — a default-on side channel describing who the agent talks to.

Both published distributions declare unbounded dependency floors (uagents-core >=0.4.8, cosmpy >=0.12.1, and ecdsa/httpx/requests in uagents-core), so a downstream install can resolve a future major the project never tested, and no dependency, container or code scanning job exists in the repository.
The project's own builds are reproducible: lockfiles are committed for both packages and CI installs with uv sync --locked across a four-version Python matrix.

attack_paths.name: Default inspector to message disclosure and re-registration

steps.summary: the inspector ships enabled, registering four REST endpoints and switching on the payload cache
the reserved-endpoint guard reads a client value uvicorn rewrites from any peer's X-Forwarded-For, and wildcard CORS opens the same paths to any web origin
GET /messages returns the whole cached envelope history, payloads included
POST /connect re-registers the agent at a caller-supplied endpoint using the token in the request body

attack_paths.name: Unverified or replayed message reaching the wallet

steps.summary: a sender that calls itself user... has its envelope dispatched without any signature check
for signed senders, expires and nonce are never checked, so one captured envelope replays indefinitely
the handler is selected on schema digest alone — no allowlist, no quota, no per-sender state
the handler that runs holds an unrestricted wallet and ledger client with no approval gate to clear
a successfully handled message writes no log record, so driven handler activity is invisible
no alert or halt primitive exists for repeated verification failures or wallet movement to bind to
update_agent_status suppresses every exception, so even a failed deregistration produces no record

notes.lane_fit: Strained in three places. (1) uagents is a framework, not a deployed agent: user_inputs holds peer agents, a self-declared user-address class and the operator rather than human end users, and the agent's real application handlers are operator code that does not exist in this tree. (2) The outbound dispenser/resolver, the mailbox client and the registration policies are in-process library modules, but they are the channel connectors to Almanac, Agentverse and peers, so they sit in client_adapters rather than agent_core — the split between 'adapter' and 'core' is a judgement call here, not a structural fact. (3) The wallet is placed in tools_mcp as the capability handlers invoke, though it is an in-process property of the Agent object; and the inspector endpoints are carved out of agent.py into client_adapters because their trust consequence is a control plane, not orchestration.
notes.omissions: The uagents-adapter package (a2a_inbound/a2a_outbound bridges, an MCP adapter, langchain and crewai tool wrappers) and uagents-ai-engine are present in the tree but were outside the scanned subject and would push the graph past the node budget, so their MCP/A2A surfaces are excluded rather than half-modelled — a real A2A and MCP trust surface this graph does not show. Bureau (multi-agent runner), Dispatcher, Context, Protocol and the types module's protocol plumbing are folded into the orchestrator node per the framework-internals rule. The chat-agent LLM path (experimental/chat_agent) is modelled from code but carries no finding ids because the scan's subject was the base runtime with no LLM, so all three of its threats are residual by construction, not by judgement. QuotaProtocol is an edgeless node: it is a shipped control that no Agent code path constructs. The supply-chain boundary is edgeless by design (repo posture, no data flow). Boundary ids are all archetypes from the menu; no coined ids were needed. One ID-rule ambiguity: the inspector endpoints are a same-file split of agent.py whose defining section is a conditional block rather than a single function, so the prefix was taken from the flag/section name (agent inspector) — another run could plausibly prefix it from one of the handler functions instead.
